newsitem.title: LEBANON: Witness tells Beirut court of anti-Syrian attack.
newsitem.headline: Witness tells Beirut court of anti-Syrian attack.

text.p: A witness told a Beirut military court on Monday he had been asked by a Lebanese man standing trial for collaboration with Israel to assassinate a top Syrian military official in Lebanon.

Tony Kazaan, a Lebanese man, told the court he was approached by Camille al-Rami in 1988 and asked to "find a suitable time" to plant a bomb to kill Brigadier Ghazi Kenaan, head of Syrian military intelligence in Lebanon.
Rami, a former Lebanese army sergeant, and two others, including a former army lieutenant-colonel, have been charged with planning the failed attempt on Kenaan's life.
They are among 25 Lebanese who went on trial in October facing possible death penalties on charges of collaborating with Israel. Twenty-one of the suspects are being tried in absentia.
Lebanon and Israel are in a state of war despite more than five years of on-off peace talks.

Kazaan said Rami also asked him to watch the movements of Elias Hobeika, a former rightwing Christian chieftain opposed to Syria who turned pro-Syrian after his 1986 ouster from the militia, in order to liquidate him in a bomb attack.

Rami asked Kazaan to supply the intelligence on Kenaan and Hobeika for the Christian Lebanese Forces militia, which was led by Hobeika before his ouster, Kazaan said. Hobeika has been a government minister since late 1990.
